name: Adaptive reuse
summary: Conversion cost (typically office-to-residential) is driven by floor-plate depth (light/air, need for light wells), plumbing riser density for new kitchens/baths, window and facade replacement, hazardous-material abatement, code upgrades (sprinklers, egress, seismic) and historic constraints. Public hard-cost data is thin: a 2025 NYC practitioner range ($300-375/SF hard) and Chicago LaSalle-corridor public budgets (total development cost $372k-$625k/unit, ~$387/SF for the Field Building). The national default is a derived regional normalization of those — medium-low confidence.

typicalSize.method: Downtown office conversions commonly 100k-650k SF (Field Building 624k SF of vacant office, e3); smaller mid-rise/warehouse conversions 30-100k SF. Mid 200k SF is judgment.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Downtown conversions usually rely on existing/nearby garages; 0-0.8 spaces per 1,000 SF (judgment).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hand-normalized to a national basis (stated per README rule 3): NYC office-to-residential conversion 'runs $300 to $375 per square foot, including all hard costs' (e1, 2025); midpoint $337.5 / NY-NewYorkCity regional factor 1.32 (_indices/regional.json) = ~$256 -> mid $250. Cross-check: Chicago Field Building total project $241.5M / 624k SF = $387/SF (e3) incl. acquisition and soft costs; at a ~0.55-0.65 hard share that is ~$215-250/SF in Chicago (factor 1.21) -> ~$180-210 national, so $250 sits slightly high, reflecting deeper-plate and historic conversions. Low $150 = shallow-plate mid-rise or warehouse/loft conversion reusing MEP; high $400 = gateway-city historic tower (top of e1 range).

scope.notes: Contractor price for interior demolition, abatement (typical), new partitions/units, new kitchens/baths and plumbing risers, new HVAC, electrical, sprinklers, window replacement, roof/facade repairs, elevator modernization, incl. GC/OH&P. Excludes acquisition, soft costs, FF&E, light-well cuts, seismic retrofit and major facade recladding (line items). Minimal sitework (urban infill).

qualityTiers.method: low/mid = 150/250 = 0.6 (rounded 0.65); high/mid = 400/250 = 1.6; premium ~ top of NYC range normalized (375/1.32 = 284 -> 1.14) plus amenity package -> 1.3 (judgment).

systemSplit.method: No public elemental breakdown found. Derived from a residential fit-out profile with conversion-specific shifts: demolition/abatement (02) 8%; window replacement (08) 10%; plumbing (22) 10% and HVAC (23) 10% for new risers and unit systems; finishes (09) 17%; structure (03/05) only 5% (reused frame, slab penetrations); elevator modernization (14) 2%; GC (01) 10%. Verify against a conversion schedule of values.

lineItems.name: Hazardous materials abatement (asbestos, lead, PCB caulk)

cost.method: Estimating judgment: pre-1980 office buildings commonly carry ACM in fireproofing/floor tile; range from limited spot abatement to full fireproofing removal. Requires a hazmat survey.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of division 02 share; increase when the survey shows sprayed fireproofing ACM.

lineItems.name: Light well / atrium cut through deep floor plates

cost.method: Estimating judgment expressed per SF of total building GFA: slab demolition, new edge framing, new interior curtain wall and lost rentable area. Only for floor plates deeper than ~45-50 ft from window to core.

lineItems.name: Facade recladding / new curtain wall (beyond window replacement)

cost.method: Estimating judgment per SF of GFA (facade area ~0.4-0.6 x GFA at ~$80-150/SF of wall). Only when operable windows/energy code require a new envelope.

lineItems.notes: Off by default; window replacement is in baseline.

lineItems.name: Seismic / structural retrofit triggered by change of occupancy

cost.method: Estimating judgment; mainly West Coast and for unreinforced masonry. Off by default.

lineItems.notes: Switch on in high seismic zones.

lineItems.name: Historic preservation premium (restoration of character-defining features)

cost.method: Estimating judgment for Secretary of the Interior Standards work (restored windows, lobbies, ornament). Often offset by historic tax credits — Field Building used city subsidies and historic tax credits (e3).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Amenity/lobby furniture spread over residential GFA (~$3-12k per unit / ~1,100-1,300 SF) — judgment.

pctOfHard.method: Conversions carry higher design and investigation costs than new build (existing-conditions survey, hazmat survey, structural assessment, code consultant, historic consultant). PHFA allows a higher architect-fee curve for 'Rehabilitation and Restoration' (incl. conversion from another use) than for regular new construction (_common/soft-costs.json#e4). Range judgment, mid 24%.

softCosts.notes: Excludes acquisition; Morgan Stanley's widely cited $685/SF (e4) is acquisition + conversion.

hard.method: State HFAs require a 10% construction contingency for rehabilitation (DSHA, e3) and for 'rehabilitation and preservation developments' (PHFA, e4; PHFA defines rehabilitation and restoration to include conversion from another use). 15% for historic or poorly documented buildings.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Excluding acquisition: low $150 x 1.18 = $177; high $400 x 1.32 x 1.12 = ~$590. Field Building TDC incl. acquisition $387/SF (e3) and Morgan Stanley $685/SF acquisition + conversion (e4) bracket the upper end.

source.title: The Top Twelve Questions About Office-to-Residential Conversions

evidence.quote: converting an existing office property generally runs $300 to $375 per square foot, including all hard costs.
evidence.scopeNotes: Same article: ground-up residential tower $450-500/SF plus $75-100/SF demolition. Practitioner trade article, not a cost-consultant survey.

source.title: LaSalle Street Office Conversion Plans Advance for Four Developments

evidence.quote: 208 S. LaSalle St ... $123 million ... 226 apartments ... 30 N. LaSalle St ... $130 million ... 349 ... 79 W. Monroe St ... $64.2 million ... 117 apartments ... 111 W. Monroe St ... $203 million ... 345 ... a 228-room hotel
evidence.scopeNotes: Total development cost incl. acquisition and soft costs. Per unit (our arithmetic): 208 S LaSalle $544k, 30 N LaSalle $372k, 79 W Monroe $549k; 111 W Monroe $588k incl. hotel (overstated).

source.title: LaSalle Street Reinvention Gains Steam As Field Building Heads For Conversion

evidence.quote: the largest total project cost at $241.5M ... 386 residential units ... 92K SF of commercial space ... 624K SF of vacant office space ... $98M in city subsidies and historic tax credits
evidence.scopeNotes: $241.5M / 624k SF = $387/SF; / 386 units = $626k/unit (our arithmetic). Total project cost incl. acquisition/soft; historic building.

source.title: Empty Offices Are Becoming Apartments, Turning Vacancy Into Value

evidence.quote: The average cost of converting an office building into residential units is approximately $685 per square foot.
evidence.scopeNotes: Secondary citation of Morgan Stanley research; per search excerpt the figure covers acquiring and then converting. Same article: adaptive reuse 'can be 30% less expensive per unit' than new builds.

openQuestions: Obtain a cost-consultant conversion benchmark (Cumming, RLB, Gensler conversion studies) with hard cost separated from acquisition.
Get hard-cost lines from public LaSalle Reimagined TIF redevelopment agreements (city council packets) to replace the hard-share assumption.
Line-item costs (abatement, light wells, recladding, seismic) are estimating judgment — source unit costs.
